result.title: Reliability-Consistent Appearance Modeling for RGB-Infrared Multi-Object Tracking
result.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
result.summary: Recent RGB-infrared multi-object tracking (MOT) methods have substantially improved cross-modal representation learning and multimodal information integration. However, most existing methods compress RGB and infrared evidence into a unified descriptor. When one modality is temporarily degraded, the tracker can no longer regulate its contribution separately; unreliable evidence may distort association and contaminate appearance memory. We therefore propose RCA-MOT, a reliability-consistent appearance modeling framework that preserves cross-modal complementarity while retaining post-representation evidence controllability. RGB-specific, infrared-specific, and fused identity representations are maintained as jointly accessible appearance states. For each detection, a simple training-free target-scene estimator produces branch-wise appearance reliability used across the two temporal roles of appearance: relative reliability regulates different identity branches, absolute reliability calibrates borderline candidates near the ReID acceptance boundary, and the same branch-wise reliability controls how strongly matched descriptors update historical appearance memory. The individual components are intentionally simple, focusing evaluation on reliability-controllable appearance organization rather than elaborate fusion or learned reliability-estimation modules. RCA-MOT sets new SOTA results on VT-MOT and UniRTL, improving the previous best HOTA by 5.402/6.075 points and IDF1 by 11.549/12.789 points, respectively, while post-hoc analyses further validate reliability as an informative control signal. Code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RCA-MOT：不再把 RGB 与红外证据压成单一描述子，而是并行保留 RGB 专属、红外专属与融合三种外观状态，用免训练的可靠性估计调节分支权重、校准 ReID 接受边界附近的候选并控制历史外观记忆的更新强度，在 VT-MOT 与 UniRTL 上取得 SOTA。
